hot.title: Qwen-AgentWorld: Language World Models for General Agents
hot.summary: Qwen-AgentWorld introduces a family of language world models (LWMs) that simulate diverse agentic environments, surpassing frontier LLMs on the AgentWorldBench and improving agent performance across various downstream tasks. These models enhance agent learning through scalable, controllable simulation and by integrating internal predictive reasoning for action refinement.

hot.title: Unlimited OCR Works
hot.summary: Unlimited OCR introduces a model for one-shot, long-horizon parsing of multi-page documents, employing a Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA) mechanism to maintain a constant KV cache size and stable inference speed. The model achieved an overall score of 93.23% on OmniDocBench v1.5, representing a 6.22 percentage point improvement over its baseline, while efficiently processing continuous document streams.

hot.title: Tmax: A simple recipe for terminal agents
hot.summary: Researchers at the Allen Institute for AI and the University of Washington developed TMAX-15K, a large and diverse dataset of complex terminal tasks, alongside a simple reinforcement learning (RL) training recipe for open-weight language models. This approach enabled TMAX-9B to achieve 27.2% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, making it the top-performing open-weight model under 10 billion parameters at the time of publication and surpassing several larger models.

hot.title: OpenThoughts-Agent: Data Recipes for Agentic Models
hot.summary: This research systematically investigates and establishes an open data curation pipeline for training broadly capable agentic language models, identifying effective strategies for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data and demonstrating its efficacy with a new dataset that improves agentic model performance. The study also explores reinforcement learning (RL) data curation, finding that specific RL data sources can induce exploratory agent behaviors and further enhance capabilities when combined with SFT.

hot.title: JAXBench: Benchmarking Autonomous TPU Kernel Optimization
hot.summary: JAXBench introduces a TPU-native benchmark suite to evaluate autonomous kernel optimization methods, featuring 50 JAX workloads derived from production LLMs and providing device-side profiling for accurate measurement. The benchmark demonstrates that state-of-the-art LLM agents can achieve a 1.36x geomean speedup over XLA compilation, reaching about 77% of hand-tuned Pallas kernel performance on specific compute-bound tasks.

hot.title: Tapered Language Models
hot.summary: This work introduces Tapered Language Models (TLMs), an architectural principle that monotonically decreases a parameter-bearing component's capacity, specifically MLP width, across model depth while maintaining a fixed total parameter budget. The approach consistently improved average commonsense reasoning accuracy and perplexity across diverse architectures and scales, achieving up to 1.84 perplexity points improvement on a 440M Transformer compared to uniform baselines.

hot.title: Agent-as-a-Router: Agentic Model Routing for Coding Tasks
hot.summary: The Agent-as-a-Router framework, instantiated as ACRouter, introduces a dynamic, self-adaptive model routing paradigm for coding tasks, continuously learning from execution-grounded feedback to select optimal Large Language Models. This approach achieves the lowest cumulative regret and improved cost-efficiency on a new benchmark, CodeRouterBench, demonstrating strong generalization to out-of-distribution agentic programming tasks.

hot.title: ParallelKernelBench: Can LLMs Write Fast Multi-GPU Kernels?
hot.summary: ParallelKernelBench (PKB), a new benchmark and evaluation framework, assesses the ability of large language models (LLMs) to generate high-performance multi-GPU kernels. The evaluation shows frontier LLMs struggle with complex distributed parallelism, achieving limited correctness and speedup in single-shot settings, though they occasionally produce 'net new' kernels that outperform PyTorch+NCCL baselines for specific workloads.

hot.title: InSight: Self-Guided Skill Acquisition via Steerable VLAs
hot.summary: INSIGHT introduces a framework for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to autonomously acquire new manipulation skills by identifying missing primitive actions and generating their own training data. The system enables robots to continually expand their learned skill vocabulary, achieving high success rates in novel tasks while retaining prior capabilities and improving execution efficiency.

hot.title: Wan-Streamer v0.1: End-to-end Real-time Interactive Foundation Models
hot.summary: Wan-Streamer v0.1 from Alibaba Group presents a unified causal Transformer for real-time, full-duplex audio-visual interaction, achieving a model-side response latency of 200 ms and total interaction latency of 550 ms with continuous visible behavior and native cross-modal synchronization at 192p resolution.

hot.title: World Value Models for Robotic Manipulation
hot.summary: This research introduces the World Value Model (WVM), which repurposes spatiotemporal priors from video world models to achieve a generalist robotic value estimator with enhanced temporal understanding. It establishes a new evaluation benchmark, Suboptimal-Value-Bench, demonstrating WVM's superior ability to track task progress in suboptimal scenarios and guide robust policy learning from mixed-quality data.

hot.title: NatureBench: Can Coding Agents Match the Published SOTA of Nature-Family Papers?
hot.summary: This work introduces NatureBench, a benchmark and automated pipeline (NatureGym), to evaluate AI coding agents' ability to surpass published scientific state-of-the-art (SOTA) across 90 tasks derived from Nature-family papers. It finds that current frontier agents achieve limited SOTA surpassing (max 17.8% of tasks) and moderate SOTA matching (max 47.8%), relying primarily on generic ML engineering rather than novel scientific discovery.

hot.title: MAS-PromptBench: When Does Prompt Optimization Improve Multi-Agent LLM Systems?
hot.summary: A new benchmark, MAS-PromptBench, systematically quantifies the effects of prompt optimization in multi-agent LLM systems, revealing that while optimization can improve performance by up to 24.0 percentage points in specific setups, it can also cause degradations of up to 16.0 points, with outcomes heavily influenced by task type, communication structure, and team size.

hot.title: Self-Compacting Language Model Agents
hot.summary: A training-free framework called SELFCOMPACT enables large language model (LLM) agents to autonomously manage their context by adaptively deciding when and what to summarize using a rubric-based mechanism. This approach improves task performance by up to 18.1 points on math reasoning and 9.2 points on agentic search, while reducing token costs by 33-67%.

hot.title: Lift4D: Harmonizing Single-View 3D Estimation for 4D Reconstruction In-the-Wild
hot.summary: Carnegie Mellon University researchers developed Lift4D, a test-time optimization framework that reconstructs complete 4D (3D geometry and motion) representations of dynamic, non-rigid objects from monocular in-the-wild videos. The system integrates causal latent propagation for temporal consistency and occlusion-aware appearance refinement with view-conditioned diffusion priors, demonstrating improved perceptual quality, temporal coherence, and semantic fidelity over prior methods on synthetic and real-world datasets.

hot.title: HoloAgent-0: A Unified Embodied Agent Framework with 3D Spatial Memory
hot.summary: HoloAgent-0, a unified embodied agent framework developed by Horizon Robotics and D-Robotics Robotics, bridges the divide between large language model reasoning and real-world physical robot execution. It integrates persistent 3D spatial memory and a structured skill interface to facilitate robust, closed-loop task execution, demonstrating high success rates in real-robot navigation and competitive performance in semantic mapping.

hot.title: MeshFlow: Mesh Generation with Equivariant Flow Matching
hot.summary: MeshFlow generates high-quality 3D triangle meshes using an equivariant optimal-transport flow matching model applied to a triangle soup representation. The method achieves an 18.55x speedup over autoregressive baselines, generating meshes in under a second, while improving fidelity and reducing self-intersections to 7.97% on categories like Lamp.

hot.title: TuringViT: Making SOTA Vision Transformers Accessible to All
hot.summary: The Foundation Model Team at Xpeng Inc. introduced TuringViT, a Vision Transformer designed for enhanced accessibility of state-of-the-art visual encoders through an efficient linear-attention-dominant architecture, a sophisticated data curation pipeline, and native dynamic-resolution training. This system achieved competitive performance on vision and multimodal benchmarks using substantially less pre-training data and demonstrated improved inference efficiency for high-resolution inputs.

hot.title: SeFi-Image: A Text-to-Image Foundation Model with Semantic-First Diffusion
hot.summary: SeFi-Image is a text-to-image foundation model that leverages a Semantic-First Diffusion paradigm to achieve high-quality image generation. The model produces competitive or superior results on benchmarks for prompt following, text rendering, and bilingual generation, notably with substantially reduced training computational cost compared to other leading models.

hot.title: DiffusionBench: On Holistic Evaluation of Diffusion Transformers
hot.summary: Researchers introduce NANOGEN, a unified framework for Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) that streamlines evaluation across ImageNet and text-to-image (T2I) generation tasks. Their findings reveal a limited correlation between ImageNet-FID and T2I performance, leading to the proposal of DIFFUSIONBENCH for a more comprehensive assessment of DiT capabilities.

likes.title: S-Agent: Spatial Tool-Use Elicits Reasoning for Spatial Intelligence
likes.summary: S-AGENT introduces a framework for spatial intelligence in Vision-Language Models, enabling them to reason over continuous, evolving 3D environments by accumulating spatio-temporal evidence. This is achieved through a VLM planner orchestrating hierarchical spatial tools and dual memory systems, leading to improved performance on multi-image and video spatial reasoning benchmarks.

likes.title: MemoryWAM: Efficient World Action Modeling with Persistent Memory
likes.summary: A hybrid memory design is presented for World Action Models, enabling efficient and persistent long-range context for robotic manipulation in memory-dependent tasks. This approach achieves comparable or superior performance to full-history models on benchmarks like RMBench and real-world scenarios while significantly reducing inference latency and GPU memory consumption.

likes.title: How Transparent is DiffusionGemma?
likes.summary: Engels et al. (2026) investigate the transparency of DiffusionGemma, a text diffusion model, finding it achieves comparable monitorability to autoregressive models like Gemma 4. The study demonstrates that its latent intermediate states can be made largely interpretable, significantly reducing its 'opaque serial depth' and revealing unique non-autoregressive reasoning patterns.

likes.title: VIMPO: Value-Implicit Policy Optimization for LLMs
likes.summary: VIMPO introduces a policy optimization framework for large language models that bridges the simplicity of critic-free methods with the fine-grained credit assignment of actor-critic approaches. The method, developed at UC Berkeley and Yale, achieves higher validation accuracy on mathematical reasoning benchmarks and demonstrates greater robustness to noisy reward signals compared to existing critic-free baselines.

likes.title: Current World Models Lack a Persistent State Core
likes.summary: WRBench, a diagnostic benchmark for evaluating video generation models, reveals that current systems struggle to maintain a consistently evolving world state independent of observation. It exposes a "preservation–access–re-observed-consistency gap," where models often fail to correctly advance object states and events when out of view, performing as "tracking shots" instead of genuine world models.

likes.title: HumanScale: Egocentric Human Video Can Outperform Real-Robot Data for Embodied Pretraining
likes.summary: A study empirically compares egocentric human video and real-robot data for embodied pretraining, demonstrating that human video yields superior generalization to unseen tasks and enhanced robustness in real-world robot deployment, even with pseudo-action labels. The research finds that egocentric data scales predictably and fosters a more effective "open-world prior" for robotic policies.

likes.title: ENPIRE: Agentic Robot Policy Self-Improvement in the Real World
likes.summary: ENPIRE provides a framework for autonomous robot policy self-improvement, allowing coding agents to refine dexterous manipulation skills directly on physical robots without extensive human supervision. The system achieves up to 99% success rates on challenging real-world tasks like pin insertion and zip-tie cutting, utilizing automated environment feedback and parallelized learning across robot fleets.

likes.title: World Action Models: A Survey
likes.summary: The survey by Shen et al. addresses the inconsistent terminology and blurred boundaries in the rapidly evolving field of World Action Models (WAMs) in embodied AI. It provides a systematic framework, classifying WAMs into three design philosophies and a four-axis component-level anatomy, revealing pervasive design trade-offs between representational richness and computational efficiency.

likes.title: Sensorimotor World Models: Perception for Action via Inverse Dynamics
likes.summary: Researchers at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems developed Sensorimotor World Models (SMWM), which learn compact, action-aligned latent states from high-dimensional observations by incorporating inverse dynamics regularization. This method effectively prevents representation collapse during end-to-end training and achieves a 84% success rate on a 3D manipulation task, outperforming the SIGReg baseline at 59%, while forming highly interpretable latent spaces.

likes.title: Finetuning Vision-Language-Action Models Requires Fewer Layers Than You Think
likes.summary: Researchers introduced CKA-guided Layer Pruning (CLP), a method that identifies and removes redundant transformer layers in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models like \u03c00 and GR00T-N1.5. This training-free approach compresses model depth by up to 50%, reduces training time by up to 1.94x, and often enhances real-world task success rates without compromising policy performance.

likes.title: EventVLA: Event-Driven Visual Evidence Memory for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Policies
likes.summary: EventVLA introduces an end-to-end framework that equips Vision-Language-Action policies with a sparse, event-driven visual memory, enabling robust performance on long-horizon, non-Markovian robotic manipulation tasks. The approach achieved an average 75.2% success rate on the new RoboTwin-MeM benchmark and up to 90% success in real-world bimanual tasks.

likes.title: CrossFlow: One-Step Generation Across Latent and Pixel Spaces
likes.summary: CrossFlow introduces a one-step generative framework that maps noisy latent inputs directly to pixel-space images in a single function evaluation, eliminating the need for a separate decoder. The largest model, CrossFlow-XL, achieved a Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) of 1.62 on ImageNet-1k at 256x256 resolution, demonstrating competitive image quality with significantly reduced inference steps.

likes.title: CalTennis: Large Multi-View Tennis Video Dataset and Benchmark of Monocular-to-3D Pose Estimation
likes.summary: Researchers from the California Institute of Technology introduce CalTennis, a large multi-view tennis video dataset, and a label-free evaluation framework for monocular-to-3D pose estimation. Their benchmark reveals that state-of-the-art models exhibit persistent inconsistencies in metric-scale depth, foot contact, and body shape estimation in unconstrained athletic settings, while showing more robust relative joint-angle recovery.
